learning: If the oval keeps 17 or more finishes with oscillation under about 0.25, the narrower track is paying off on the s-bend. If the oval oscillation rises above 0.3, the next step is kd 0.5 before any geometry change. If the slalom stays near 0.18, the limit is probably speed or lag, so test base_speed or the wheel_radius lever.
notes: Builder's geometry adopted unchanged, with wheel_track 0.09 to 0.08 m as proposed. Controller kept from iteration 4 except kd raised from 0.4 to 0.45 to damp the extra turn response from the narrower track.
rationale: Iteration 4 (score 404.6) is the best evidence: at wheel_track 0.09 m and y=0.08 m the oval finished 20 of 20 (rms 0.023, max_error 0.038, steering_oscillation 0.205), and s-bend progress reached 0.486. The slalom is flat at progress 0.177 and still ends off track at max_error about 0.063. The Builder's proposal changes only wheel_track, from 0.09 to 0.08 m, which raises turn rate per unit of turn by about 12.5%. The sensing array, sensor_size, wheel_radius, mass and body dimensions are therefore kept exactly as proposed. For the controller, the narrower track makes the same command turn harder, so the oval's oscillation risk rises. I keep kp at 2.5 and base_speed at 1.7, which both worked in iterations 3 and 4, and raise kd modestly from 0.4 to 0.45 to damp that extra turn response. ki stays at 0.05 and line_loss stays last_direction, which recovered the tape edge in every race so far. The main uncertainty is whether the oval holds its finishes with the higher effective gain; the slalom may stay near 0.18 if its limit is speed or lag rather than turn rate.
